NCC recalls Range Rover Sport and Volkswagen Transporter vehicles
Image:
Supplied
The
National Consumer Commission
(NCC) has announced the recall of 389 Range Rover Sport and Volkswagen Transporter vehicles over potentially cracked rear subframes and Bridgestone tyres that could shed their tread.
The recall affects 82 Range Rover Sport SV vehicles manufactured between 3 October 2023 and 24 June 2026.
The
NCC
said Jaguar Land Rover Limited identified the potential presence of cracks in the rear subframes of certain vehicles following a renewed analysis of supplier imaging records.
The affected vehicles are from the 2024 to 2026 model years and were sold through Jaguar Land Rover dealerships in South Africa.
According to Jaguar Land Rover Limited, a concern has been identified where, on certain Range Rover Sport SV vehicles, renewed analysis of supplier imaging history has detected the potential presence of cracks on the rear subframe for some vehicles.
"In the event of a crack, a crack on the rear subframe can compromise the structural integrity of the vehicle and can increase the risk of occupant injury. In addition, over time a crack could propagate and cause a deterioration in design strength," the NCC said.
Vehicles confirmed to have cracks will have their rear subframes replaced. Vehicles that could not be assessed through photographic inspections will undergo physical inspections, with replacement carried out if cracks are detected.
The second recall affects 307 Volkswagen Transporter vehicles fitted with Bridgestone Duravis R660 ECO tyres, size 215/60 R17C 109/107T.
Volkswagen Group Africa said six of the affected vehicles had been exported to Namibia. The remaining vehicles were supplied for sale in South Africa through approved dealerships between 6 February 2025 and 11 December 2025.
The tyre defect could cause sections of the tread to detach. In rare cases, the entire tread could separate.
Volkswagen warned that this could cause the tyre to lose air gradually or suddenly, affecting vehicle handling and increasing the risk of vehicle damage or personal injury.
Owners of affected vehicles should contact their nearest approved Jaguar Land Rover or Volkswagen dealership to arrange an inspection and, where necessary, repairs.
NCC said all inspections and recall repairs will be carried out free of charge.

Safety defects linked to potential crashes, injuries and vehicle damage have triggered recalls affecting nearly 400 Range Rover Sport and Volkswagen Transporter vehicles across South Africa.
The National Consumer Commission (NCC) has announced two vehicle safety recalls involving 82 Range Rover Sport SV vehicles and 307 Volkswagen Transporter vehicles after manufacturers identified defects that could affect vehicle safety.
Range Rover Sport recall
NCC spokesperson Phetho Ntaba said Jaguar Land Rover Limited is recalling 82 Range Rover Sport SV vehicles from the 2024 to 2026 model years manufactured between 3 October 2023 and 24 June 2026 and sold through dealers nationwide.
“The manufacturer said renewed analysis of supplier imaging history identified the potential presence of cracks in the rear subframe of some vehicles.”
According to the NCC, a crack in the rear subframe could compromise the vehicle’s structural integrity, increase the risk of occupant injury and, over time, worsen to the point where it increases the risk of a crash.

“Vehicles found to have a crack will have the rear subframe replaced, while those that could not be assessed through photographic inspection will undergo further inspection and repairs where necessary,” Ntaba said.
Volkswagen Transporter recall
Volkswagen Group Africa (VWGA) is recalling 307 Volkswagen Transporter vehicles fitted with Bridgestone Duravis R660 ECO tyres. Six of the affected vehicles were exported to Namibia.
Ntaba said the recalled vehicles were sold through approved Volkswagen dealers between 6 February 2025 and 11 December 2025.
“Volkswagen said parts of the tyre tread may detach and, in rare cases, separate completely, potentially causing a gradual or sudden loss of air pressure.”
The defect could adversely affect vehicle handling, posing a risk of vehicle damage and personal injury.

What should owners do?
The NCC has advised owners of affected vehicles to contact their nearest approved Jaguar Land Rover or Volkswagen dealer to arrange inspections and any necessary repairs.
All recall-related inspections and repairs will be carried out free of charge.
At a glance
82 Range Rover Sport SV vehicles recalled
307 Volkswagen Transporter vehicles recalled
Range Rover recall linked to potential rear subframe cracks
Volkswagen recall linked to tyre tread separation
All inspections and repairs are free of charge
Consumers who own affected vehicles are encouraged to contact their nearest authorised dealership as soon as possible to arrange the necessary corrective action.
